summary: GRAVEYARD expectations/execution revision covered every b03 company and incorporated newer same-cycle Alpha primary financial evidence. AUR and SMR now have sufficient capitalization/runway denominators for lane-level Chief treatment; financing dependence remains a material execution risk rather than an unresolved gate. SERV remains blocked only on current concentration/post-financing runway. Missing canonical live price, consensus and crowding data remains explicit non-gating unknown.

materialFindings.finding: Execution evidence remains strong, while geographic semiconductor concentration raises expectation risk if AI-test demand is extrapolated as structurally diversified.
Automation recovery can be treated as execution evidence, but current issuer-primary financial normalization remains an underwriting task; no live valuation input is fabricated.
FY2025 revenue growth, operating cash flow and new OEM/robotaxi program evidence strengthen execution credibility while ASP/mix economics remain an explicit counterweight.
Deployment narrative remains highly expectation-sensitive because current customer concentration and post-financing runway are not refreshed; execution/survival treatment is not reproducible yet.

June 2026 $1.217B cash plus short-term investments versus six-month $493M net loss and only $3M revenue quantifies runway and commercialization gap. Shares outstanding increased, so execution credit must remain separate from dilution risk.

Order/backlog acceleration across electrical and aerospace markets supports delivery credibility; elevated data-center expectations and acquisition contribution remain opportunity-layer considerations.
Backlog supports visibility but not automatic valuation upside; conversion cadence and project controls remain execution variables.
Primary backlog growth and first data-center megaproject order validate demand capture while large-award concentration makes conversion lumpy.
Contract duration and nuclear/data-center positioning support execution narrative; integration/regulatory timing remains event risk and current financial dossier remains an underwriting task.
Long-duration PPAs support visibility while hedge/basis/integration sensitivities remain execution risks; current financial dossier remains an underwriting task.
Demand/backlog narrative remains credible but heterogeneous backlog quality prevents simplistic expectation extrapolation; current financial refresh remains underwriting-specific.

FY2025 $1.300B net common-stock issuance proceeds versus $459.6M operating cash use provides a reproducible financing/runway denominator. Execution remains pre-scale and flagship deployment nonbinding, but the lane can now pass the facts to Chief without blocking on missing capitalization.

gatingGaps: current customer concentration and post-financing runway needed for reproducible execution/financing-risk treatment

contradictions: AUR's substantial runway coexists with minimal revenue, high cash use and rising share count.
SMR liquidity is high but materially equity-financed, so runway and dilution must be assessed jointly.
unknowns: Normalized live price, consensus, crowding and short-interest inputs are not canonical T0 inputs in this pass and remain unknown rather than fabricated.
peerRequests: Company-underwriting/source-integrity: finish SERV current concentration/runway; Chief: treat AUR/SMR financing dependence explicitly without re-blocking them solely for future economic uncertainty.
